Need evaluate every story PP-001 to PP-053 for Atomic criterion: story expresses requirement for exactly one feature; violation when combines two or more independently implementable, testable, prioritizable features. Need be careful. We need assess each story from own text. Need produce 53 objects. Need no prose outside JSON.

Need decide for each. Let's parse backlog.

We need judge Atomic. Usually user story format "As a ..., I want ..., so that ...". Atomic means one feature. Stories with multiple clauses may still be one feature if attributes. Need identify violations.

Let's list stories:

PP-001: As moderator, I want to create a new game by entering a name and an optional description, so that I can start inviting estimators.
This is one feature: create game with fields name and optional description. Entering name and optional description are attributes of one feature. No violation.

PP-002: invite estimators by giving URL where they can access game, so we can start game. One feature.

PP-003: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field, so estimate it. One feature.

PP-004: see all items we try to estimate this session, so answer questions. One feature.

PP-005: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated, so team sees item and can estimate. This includes select item to be estimated or re-estimated—maybe same feature? Selecting item for estimation vs re-estimation. It is one action "select an item" with purpose. "or re-estimated" is scenario, not two features. No violation likely.

PP-006: add an item to list, one feature.

PP-007: edit item, one feature.

PP-008: delete item, one feature.

PP-012: enter agreed-upon estimate, one feature.

PP-043: as developer, want to have written a site compliant with XHTML and CSS standards, one feature? This combines XHTML and CSS standards? Are they two independently implementable features? Hmm. The "site compliant with XHTML and CSS standards" is a single quality requirement? Atomic criterion says exactly one feature. Compliance with XHTML and CSS standards could be considered one feature "standards-compliant site" though includes two standards. Need think. The operational rule: Violation when story combines two or more independently implementable, testable, or prioritizable features. Do not flag conjunctions that merely enumerate attributes of one feature. "compliant with XHTML and CSS standards" could be a single feature of standards compliance enumerating two standards. Likely no violation because one feature: create site compliant with web standards. But could be argued two separate requirements: XHTML compliance and CSS compliance. Are they independently testable? Yes, one can validate XHTML and CSS separately. But story scope? "site compliant with XHTML and CSS standards" as a developer story likely one feature about standards compliance. We need decide. For atomic individual, likely many QUS examples consider compound "and" conjunction. Need carefully.

Need evaluate all. There may be stories with multiple features more obvious:

Is that one feature: cross-browser compatibility, or multiple features because each browser compatibility is independently testable/prioritizable? The story expresses requirement for one feature: application works in specified browsers. Multiple browsers are attributes/environments. Atomic?
